LESSON: WORD CLASS: NOUNS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.3.1: Word Class: Nouns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Word Class: Nouns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: which occur as same in both singular and plural in sentences. 1. Why is it important to use words correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences
2. use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WORD CLASS: NOUNS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Word Class: Nouns helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WORD CLASS: NOUNS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Word Class: Nouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Word Class: Nouns to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Word Class: Nouns is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Word Class: Nouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Word Class: Nouns to a partner. (skill: use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Word Class: Nouns to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences.
3. Practise this skill: use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Word Class: Nouns from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Word Class: Nouns: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Word Class: Nouns?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. which occur as same in both singular and plural in sentences. 1. Why is it important to use words correctly?
2. Which singular nouns end with letter -s?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Word Class: Nouns means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural from given sentences.
5. Be able to: use nouns which occur as same in both singular and plural to make sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
